poems.title: 月夜の浜辺
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: water's edge, where the waves break
was lying (dropped) there (historical kana for いた)
pick up (historical spelling つ for small っ)
could not bear to throw away
to soak in, to pierce (feelings, cold)

poems.paraphrase: 月の出ている夜、ボタンが一つ波打ちぎわに落ちていた。拾って何かに使おうと思ったわけではない。でも、なぜか捨てる気持ちになれず、僕はそれを着物の袂に入れた。月の夜、ボタンが一つ波打ちぎわに落ちていた。使おうと思ったわけではないが、月に向かっても波に向かっても投げることができず、僕はそれを袂に入れた。月の夜に拾ったボタンは、指先にしみ、心にしみた。月の夜に拾ったボタンを、どうして捨てることができるだろうか。
poems.gloss: On a moonlit night a single button was lying at the water's edge. I did not pick it up because I meant to use it, yet somehow I could not bring myself to throw it away, so I put it in my sleeve. The scene repeats: I could not throw it toward the moon, I could not throw it toward the waves, and I put it in my sleeve. The button I picked up on that moonlit night went deep into my fingertips and into my heart. How could I ever throw it away?
poems.note: A small, useless object becomes precious through the mood of the moonlit shore; the repetition works like a refrain. Historical kana: ゐた = いた, 拾つて = 拾って, 向つて = 向って; 捨てられようか is a rhetorical question meaning 'I could never throw it away.'

poems.title: 悲しい月夜
poems.author: 萩原朔太郎

vocabulary.gloss: is barking/howling (historical kana for いる)

poems.paraphrase: 泥棒のような野良犬が、くさった波止場の月に向かって吠えている。魂が耳をすますと、陰気な声で、黄色い娘たちが合唱している。波止場の暗い石垣のところで合唱している。いつもどうして俺はこうなのだろう。犬よ、青白く不幸な犬よ。
poems.gloss: A thieving cur is howling at the moon over the rotting wharf. When my soul listens closely, yellowish girls are singing together in gloomy voices, singing by the dark stone wall of the wharf. Why am I always like this? O dog, pale, unhappy dog.
poems.note: The howling dog mirrors the speaker's own misery, and the 'yellow girls' are a strange, unexplained image, so read them neutrally. Historical kana: ゐる = いる, たましひ = たましい, ふしあはせ = ふしあわせ.

poems.title: 白い月
poems.author: 萩原朔太郎

vocabulary.gloss: to sow (historical kana for まこう)
slender, delicate (no small kana in old spelling)

poems.paraphrase: ひどい虫歯の痛みで、はれたほっぺたを手でおさえながら、私はナツメの木の下を掘っていた。何かの草の種をまこうとして、細い指を泥だらけにしながら、冷たい地面を掘り返した。ああ、私はそれを覚えている。少し寒い日の夕方、新しい穴の底で、ミミズがちろちろと動いていた。そのとき、低い建物の後ろから、真っ白な女の耳をなでるように、つるつると月がのぼった。月がのぼった。
poems.gloss: Holding my cheek, swollen from a bad toothache, I was digging under a jujube tree. Meaning to sow the seeds of some plant, I turned over the cold ground, my slender fingers covered in mud. Ah, I remember it: at dusk on a chilly day, at the bottom of the fresh hole, an earthworm was wriggling. Just then, from behind a low building, the moon rose smoothly, as if stroking a woman's pure white ear. The moon rose.
poems.note: A childhood memory where physical pain and a sensual image of the rising moon mix. The final line 幼童思慕詩篇 ('poems of childhood longing') is a section label from the collection, not part of the poem; historical kana: ゐた = いた, やう = よう, 蒔かう = まこう.

poems.title: 月から
poems.author: 新美南吉

vocabulary.gloss: here and there, in all directions

poems.paraphrase: 月から来た猫が屋根の上にいる。屋根の上で、しっぽをぴんと立てている。月から来た鳥が木の穴にいる。穴の中から、あちこちに向かって大声で鳴いている。月から来た人が柵のところにいる。柵のところで、ナイフを抜いている。
poems.gloss: A cat that came from the moon is on the roof. From the roof it sticks its tail straight up. A bird that came from the moon is in a tree hollow. From the hollow it cries out loudly here and there. A person who came from the moon is at the fence. At the fence he is drawing a knife.
poems.note: A children's-song pattern of three parallel stanzas that turns suddenly uneasy with the knife in the last one; the poem does not explain it. Historical kana: ゐる = いる, しつぽ = しっぽ.

poems.title: お月さまを
poems.author: 新美南吉
poems.paraphrase: お月さまを見上げた。マストにのぼった船乗りが見上げた。「なんだか青い」と、そう言った。お月さまを見上げた。私が窓から、一人きりで見上げた。「お母さん、静かね」と、そう言った。
poems.gloss: Someone looked up at the moon: a sailor who had climbed the mast. 'It's somehow blue,' he said. Someone looked up at the moon: I did, alone at the window. 'Mother, it's quiet, isn't it,' I said.
poems.note: Two people in different places look at the same moon, one at sea and one at home; the mother addressed in the last line may not be present, so the tone is lonely. Historical kana: さう = そう, のぼつた = のぼった.

poems.title: 月の角笛
poems.author: 新美南吉
poems.paraphrase: 月が夜ふけに角笛を吹いた。ぽうぽうぽう。犬が野原を歩き回って鳴いた。ぎりりと時計のねじを巻いて、牧師がことことと階段を下りた。月が遠くで角笛を吹いた。ぽうぽうぽう。牛があわわと大きなあくびをした。からからと窓の戸を閉めて、「ああ、遠い」と牛乳屋が言った。
poems.gloss: Late at night the moon blew its horn: poh, poh, poh. A dog went around the field, barking. Creak, the pastor wound his clock and went clip-clop down the stairs. The moon blew its horn far away: poh, poh, poh. A cow gave a big, gaping yawn. Rattle, the milkman shut the shuttered window and said, 'Ah, it's so far away.'
poems.note: The moon's 'horn' is an imagined sound that the whole night village reacts to; the poem is built on onomatopoeia (ぽうぽう, ことこと, からら). シヤーレ is an unusual loanword, probably a kind of window shutter, so treat it as uncertain; をば is an emphatic old object marker.

poems.title: 月
poems.author: 八木重吉

vocabulary.gloss: to be shone on, lit up

poems.paraphrase: 月の光に照らされると、自然に遊びたくなってくる。そっと涙を流したり、にこにこ笑ったりして、踊りたくなる。
poems.gloss: When the moon shines on me, I find myself wanting to play, without meaning to. I quietly shed tears, or smile, and I want to dance.
poems.note: A very short, childlike poem about how moonlight brings out mixed, simple feelings; tears and smiles sit side by side. ～たくなる means 'come to want to ~'.

poems.title: 北の海
poems.author: 中原中也
poems.paraphrase: 海にいるのは、人魚ではない。海にいるのは、波だけだ。曇った北の海の空の下で、波はところどころ歯をむき出して、空をのろっている。いつ終わるのかわからない、のろいだ。海にいるのは、人魚ではない。海にいるのは、波だけだ。
poems.gloss: What is in the sea is not mermaids. What is in the sea is only waves. Under the cloudy sky of the northern sea, the waves bare their teeth here and there and curse the sky, a curse that no one knows when it will end. What is in the sea is not mermaids; it is only waves.
poems.note: The poem rejects the romantic image of mermaids for the harsh reality of the grey northern waves. Historical kana: ゐる = いる, 呪つて = 呪って; はてる is a literary verb meaning 'to end'.

poems.title: 海辺にて
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: when it comes crashing (colloquial ～てくれば)

poems.paraphrase: 波よ、波、波、ここまでおいで。波よ、波、波、つかまえてごらん。どんと打ち寄せてきたら、それ、にげた。波よ、波、波、ここまでおいで。怒ったのかい、波よ。さっと引いていくとき、砂の小山をけちらしていった。
poems.gloss: Waves, waves, waves, come over here! Waves, waves, waves, come and catch me! When one comes crashing in with a boom, there, off I run. Waves, waves, waves, come over here! Did you get angry, waves? As you drew back all at once, you kicked apart my little mound of sand.
poems.note: A child's game of tag with the waves, full of spoken, playful language; that the child is the one who runs away is implied rather than stated. つかまへて is historical kana for つかまえて, and くりや is a colloquial contraction.

poems.title: 春の海のうた
poems.author: 山村暮鳥

vocabulary.gloss: of the long days (日永, spring)
rocky shore, rocks by the sea

poems.paraphrase: 満ちたり引いたりする春の潮。日の長い春の、青い海。ひょっこりと岩が沈むと、ぴょっこりと船が浮かんできた。ぴょっこりと船が浮かぶと、ひょっこりと岩が沈んだ。岩と船のかくれんぼだ。それを見ていたカモメも、カモメ同士でかくれんぼ。ひょっこり浮かんだり沈んだりしている。
poems.gloss: The spring tide comes in and goes out. The blue sea of the long spring days. When the rocks suddenly sink, a little boat pops up. When the boat pops up, the rocks suddenly sink. The rocks and the boat are playing hide-and-seek. The gulls watching them play hide-and-seek too, bobbing up and sinking down.
poems.note: A playful nursery-rhyme view of the tide covering and uncovering the rocks while a boat rises and falls on the swell. Written all in historical kana: しほ = しお, あを = あお, しづむ = しずむ, and small kana are not used (ひよつこり = ひょっこり).

poems.title: 渚
poems.author: 山村暮鳥
poems.paraphrase: 千鳥の足あとは小さいね。夜明けの渚に出てみたかい。夜明けの渚には、どんどんと打つ波。波が消し忘れた砂の上に、千鳥の足あと。かわいいね。
poems.gloss: How small the plovers' footprints are. Have you gone out to the shore at dawn? At the dawn shore the waves pound. On the sand the waves forgot, there are plovers' footprints. How sweet they are.
poems.note: The waves wash the beach but 'forget' one patch, leaving the tiny bird tracks; the tone is gentle, spoken to a child. Sentence-final な/か give a soft, conversational feel.

poems.title: 海よ
poems.author: 三好達治

vocabulary.gloss: to bask in the sun (lit. dry one's shell)
insincerity, faithlessness (old form of 不実)

poems.paraphrase: 「門を閉じよ、心を開け」。それで私は表の戸を閉めて、裏の垣根を越えてきた。みかん畑の間を抜けて、海よ、お前の渚に、こうして私は一人で来た。かげろうが燃える初夏の小道、まぶしい砂の上で、海よ、私は何を考えようか。思い出のようにうすく曇って、青みがかった灰色にぼんやりした、遠いお前の水平線。私はお前と向き合い、世の中に背を向ける。門を閉じ、心を開いて、私はここに来た。海よ、お前の渚に、こうして私は腰を下ろし、日なたぼっこをする。空と大地、岬の先のカラスの群れ、まるく高くふくらむお前の波、胸の奥にずんと響くお前の歌声、きらきら光る真っ白な新しい季節の帆が二つ三つ。海よ、やがて私は旅立つだろう。お前のこの渚からも旅立つだろう。人の不誠実に怒ることも、自分の真実に酔うことも、その時私はやめるだろう。その日がやがて来るだろう。お前と別れるその日のために、今日私はお前をたたえて歌い、お前と遊ぶ。お前の渚で、私は今日お前と遊ぶ。
poems.gloss: 'Close the gate, open the heart...' So I shut the front of the house, climbed over the back hedge, and passed between the mandarin orchards to come alone to your shore, O sea. On the early-summer path where the heat haze shimmers, on the dazzling sand, what shall I think about, O sea? Your distant horizon is dim like a memory, a hazy bluish grey. I face you and turn my back on the world. Here on your shore I sit down and bask in the sun, with the sky and the earth, the crows on the tip of the cape, your waves swelling round and high, your song that echoes deep in my chest, and two or three sails, dazzling white and new with the season. O sea, before long I will set out on a journey, even from this shore of yours. Then I will stop being angry at people's faithlessness and stop being drunk on my own sincerity. That day will come soon. For the day I part from you, today I sing your praises and play with you on your shore.
poems.note: The sea is a place of escape from society and of quiet farewell before an unnamed 'journey' that the poem leaves open. Written in old characters and kana: 閉ぢよ = 閉じよ, かうして = こうして, だらう = だろう, 拔/徑/數/眞 are old forms of 抜/径/数/真.

poems.title: 南の海へ行きます
poems.author: 萩原朔太郎
poems.titleEn: I Am Going to the Southern Sea

vocabulary.gloss: business suit (old form of 背広)

poems.paraphrase: 長い病気の痛みも消え、浅間山の雪も消えた。お客さんたちはみな都へ帰った。庭の池には水が噴き上がり、赤い鯉もちらちら泳ぎ始めたが、私は一人ぼっちになった。なぜか泣きたくなり、センチメンタルな夕暮れになった。しくしくと物思いにふけっていると、仲のいい友だちが連れ立ってやって来て、卵のようなもの、菓子のようなもの、りんごのようなものを枕元に持ってきてくれた。ああ、それでも私はさびしい。今は一人で旅に出る。長い病気の床から離れて、つばきの花が咲く南の島へ行かなければならない。つばめのように元気に飛んで行く。今日、利根川のほとりに来てみると、だんだん春の恵みを感じる。雪割草がつぼみをふくらませるように、土はうららかに燃え上がり、西も東も雪がとけて流れ、谷を次々に流れていく。光る山の頂も、広がる桑畑も、さびしい病人の涙をさそう。しみじみ思うと、故郷の冬空は晴れていても、さびしくてたまらない。だから今はすべてのものに別れを告げ、明日はいつもの背広を着て、いつもの軽い靴をはいて、まだ見たこともない南の海へ遊びに行こう。気持ちも明るく、みなさんに別れを告げて、二月の半ばに旅立つ。小鳥がぴよぴよと空で鳴き交わしている。
poems.gloss: The pain of my long illness has faded and the snow on Mount Asama has melted too. All the guests have gone back to the capital. Water spouts up in the garden pond and red carp have begun to flicker about, but I am left all alone. Somehow I want to cry; it is a sentimental dusk. As I brood tearfully, my good friends come together and bring to my pillow things like eggs, things like sweets, things like apples. Ah, but still I am lonely. Now I go off on a journey by myself, leaving the nest of my long illness; I must go to a southern island where camellias bloom, flying off as cheerfully as a swallow. Today, coming to the banks of the Tone River, I gradually feel the blessing of spring. Like the snow-breaking flowers swelling into bud, the earth brightly stirs, the snow melts and flows east and west, running on and on through the ravines. Even the shining peaks and the spreading mulberry fields draw tears from a lonely invalid. When I think deeply, though the winter sky of my hometown is clear, I am so lonely I cannot bear it. So now I say goodbye to everything; tomorrow I will put on my usual suit and my usual light shoes and go to play by the southern sea I have never seen. In a cheerful mood I bid everyone farewell and set out in mid-February, as little birds call cheep-cheep across the sky.
poems.note: Recovery, loneliness and a hopeful departure are mixed in a long, breathless sentence chain. Historical and classical forms: けふ = きょう, やうに = ように, もたらせり = 'brought', たへざれば = 'since I cannot bear it', ねばならぬ = なければならない; せんすゐ = 泉水 (garden pond/fountain) and ふくめる (budding) are read here in their most likely sense.

poems.title: 千鳥と遊ぶ智恵子
poems.author: 高村光太郎

vocabulary.reading: ひとっこひとりいない

vocabulary.gloss: to stand still (for a long time)

poems.paraphrase: 人が一人もいない九十九里の砂浜で、智恵子は砂に座って遊んでいる。数えきれない友だちが智恵子の名前を呼ぶ。ちい、ちい、ちい。砂に小さな足あとをつけて、千鳥が智恵子に近寄ってくる。口の中でいつも何かをつぶやいている智恵子が、両手をあげて呼び返す。ちい、ちい、ちい。両手の貝を千鳥がほしがる。智恵子はそれをぱらぱらと投げる。群れで飛び立つ千鳥が智恵子を呼ぶ。人間として生きることをあっさりやめて、もう自然の向こう側へ行ってしまった智恵子の後ろ姿が、ぽつんと小さく見える。二百メートル以上離れた防風林の夕日の中で、松の花粉を浴びながら、私はいつまでも立ちつくしている。
poems.gloss: On the sandy beach of Kujukuri, where there is not a single person, Chieko sits in the sand and plays. Countless friends call her name: chii, chii, chii. Leaving tiny footprints in the sand, the plovers come up to her. Chieko, who is always murmuring something to herself, raises both hands and calls back. The plovers beg for the shells in her hands, and she tosses them out, scattering. The rising flock calls to her. Chieko, who has lightly given up the business of being human and gone off beyond, into nature, is a small lone figure seen from behind. In the evening sun of the windbreak pines, more than two hundred meters away, covered in pine pollen, I stand there without moving, for a long time.
poems.note: The poet watches his wife, who has withdrawn from ordinary human life, at one with the birds; the calm scene carries deep grief. 二丁 is an old distance (about 220 m); 寄つて = 寄って and よびかへす = よびかえす are historical spellings.

poems.title: 島
poems.author: 新美南吉

vocabulary.gloss: hummer (a device on a kite that makes a humming sound)

poems.paraphrase: ある朝、島で鯨がとれた。どの家でも鯨を食べた。ひげは、凧のうなりにするために売られていった。鯨の油は、ランプの中でりららと燃えた。どこでも鯨の話がされた。島は小さな、貧しい村だ。注：鯨のひげは、凧のうなりに使われる。
poems.gloss: One morning on the island a whale was caught. Every house ate whale. The baleen was sold off to make kite hummers. The whale oil burned in the lamps, flickering. Everywhere people talked about the whale. The island is a small, poor village. (Note: whale baleen is used for the hummers on kites.)
poems.note: A single whale becomes a big event for a poor island, used down to its whiskers and oil. The poet's own note explains 呻り (a humming strip on a kite); historical kana: まづしい = まずしい, 用ゐ = 用い.

poems.title: あどけない話
poems.author: 高村光太郎
poems.paraphrase: 智恵子は、東京には空がないと言う。本当の空が見たいと言う。私は驚いて空を見る。桜の若葉の間にあるのは、切っても切れない、昔からなじみのきれいな空だ。どんよりかすむ地平のぼやけた色は、うすいもも色の朝のしめりけだ。智恵子は遠くを見ながら言う。阿多多羅山の山の上に毎日出ている青い空が、智恵子の本当の空だと言う。子どものように無邪気な、空の話である。
poems.gloss: Chieko says there is no sky in Tokyo. She says she wants to see a real sky. Surprised, I look up at the sky. What is there between the young cherry leaves is the lovely sky I have known forever, one I could never be separated from. The dull blur along the horizon is the pale-pink dampness of morning. Looking into the distance, Chieko says the blue sky that appears every day above Mount Adatara is her real sky. It is an innocent talk about the sky.
poems.note: Chieko longs for the sky of her home region, while the poet sees nothing wrong with Tokyo's sky, which reveals her homesickness. Historical kana: いふ = いう, ゐる = いる.

poems.title: 夏は青い空に……
poems.author: 中原中也

vocabulary.gloss: face up, lying on one's back

poems.paraphrase: 夏は青い空に白い雲を浮かべ、私の嘆きを歌う。私の知らない、遠い遠い深いところで、青空は白い雲を呼んでいる。私の嘆きよ、悲しみよ、顔を上げなさい。記憶もまた去っていくのではないか。わき上がる大きな喜びの前では、人の情けも小さなものに見えるのではないか。ああ、神様、これがすべてです。尽くすこともなく、尽くされることもなく、心のままに歌う心、これこそがすべてです。空の下の林の中で、だるそうに仰向けになって目を閉じ、白い雲がお前の胸の上を流れていけば、果てしない平和がお前のものになるのではないか。
poems.gloss: Summer floats white clouds in the blue sky and sings my lament. In a far, far, far depth I do not know, the blue sky calls the white clouds. My grief, my sorrow, lift up your head. Don't memories, too, go away? Before joy that wells up, don't even human kindnesses look small? Ah, God, this is everything: a heart that sings just as it feels, neither giving itself up nor being used up, this is all there is. In the woods under the sky, lying languidly on your back with your eyes closed, if the white clouds flow over your chest, won't endless peace become yours?
poems.note: A prayer-like poem moving from grief toward calm acceptance under the summer sky. Classical forms: ～にあらずや = 'is it not ~?', 昂げよ is an imperative, 汝 (な) = 'you'; 尽すなく尽さるるなく is ambiguous (roughly 'neither exhausting nor exhausted'), and たゆけく suggests languor.

poems.title: 雲
poems.author: 中原中也
poems.paraphrase: 山の上には雲が流れていた。あの山の上で弁当を食べたこともある。女の子というものは、もともと桜の花びらのように、喜んで散っていくものだ。近い過去も遠い過去も同じことだ。近い過去はあまりにもはっきり見えすぎるし、遠い過去はもう手が届かない。山の上に寝て空を見るのも、ここにいてあの山を見るのも、結局は同じだ。動くな、動くな。ああ、枯草を背中に敷いて、ほんのり暖まっていること、空の青が少し冷たく見えること、たばこを吸うこと、それは世界で一番の幸せである。
poems.gloss: Clouds were drifting over the mountain. I once ate a packed lunch up on that mountain... Girls, by their nature, are like cherry petals: they scatter gladly. The recent past and the distant past are all the same: the recent past appears too vividly, and the distant past is already out of reach. Lying on the mountain looking at the sky, or staying here looking at the mountain, in the end it is the same. Don't move, don't move. Ah, lying warm on dry grass spread under my back, the blue of the sky looking a little cold, smoking a cigarette: this is happiness on a world scale.
poems.note: A lazy, half-ironic meditation: memory and lost love are set aside for the simple pleasure of lying in the grass. Colloquial and historical forms: おんなじこつた = おなじことだ, 遠いい is a drawn-out 遠い, 喫ふ = 吸う, ゐる = いる.

poems.title: 蒼天
poems.author: 萩原朔太郎

vocabulary.gloss: single-mindedly, with one's whole heart (一心)
face up, on one's back (historical kana)
pressing the palms together in prayer

poems.paraphrase: 心を一つにすると、仰向けになって死体のようになる。冷たく手を合わせる。欲望だけを一心に思う。キリギリスはすっかり青くなり、スズメは空の中で殺される。
poems.gloss: Being single-minded, I lie on my back like a corpse, coldly pressing my palms together. One fixed thought of lust. The grasshopper turns wholly blue, and a sparrow is killed in the sky.
poems.note: A very compressed, obscure early poem mixing prayer, desire and death under a blue sky; its logic is deliberately unclear, so the rendering is only one possible reading. Classical forms: ～なれば = 'since/when it is', 殺さる = 殺される, もはら = もっぱら.

poems.title: 空と光
poems.author: 八木重吉
poems.paraphrase: 刻みつけられた空よ。光よ。
poems.gloss: O carved sky, O light.
poems.note: A three-line poem that sees the sky and light as if sharply engraved, clear and fixed; it is ambiguous whether 彫まれたる describes only the sky or both. ～たる is the classical form of ～た used before a noun, and よ marks direct address.

poems.title: 雲
poems.author: 八木重吉
poems.paraphrase: あの雲は雲だ。あの松林も雲だ。あのあたりの人々も、雲だったらいいのになあ。
poems.gloss: That cloud is a cloud. That pine grove is a cloud too. How nice it would be if the people over there were clouds as well.
poems.note: A simple wish that everything, even people, could be as soft and free as clouds; the tone is gentle, not sarcastic. ～であればいいなあ expresses a longing wish.

poems.title: 星めぐりの歌
poems.author: 宮沢賢治
poems.paraphrase: 赤い目玉のサソリ。広げたワシの翼。青い目玉の小犬。光るヘビのとぐろ。オリオンは高いところで歌い、露と霜を落とす。アンドロメダの雲は、魚の口の形。大熊の足を北に五つのばしたところ。小熊の額の上が、空をめぐる星の目じるしだ。
poems.gloss: The scorpion with a red eye, the eagle's spread wings, the little dog with a blue eye, the coil of the snake of light. Orion sings up high and lets fall dew and frost. The cloud of Andromeda is shaped like a fish's mouth. Stretch five times the Great Bear's paw toward the north, and there, above the Little Bear's forehead, is the guide for the circling of the sky.
poems.note: A song that names constellations (Scorpius with red Antares, Aquila, Canis Minor, Serpens, Orion, the Andromeda nebula) and ends with how to find the Pole Star from the Great Bear. Historical kana: あをい = あおい, うたひ = うたい, うへ = うえ.

poems.title: 〔ま青きそらの風をふるはし〕
poems.author: 宮沢賢治
poems.titleEn: Shaking the Wind of the Deep Blue Sky
poems.paraphrase: 真っ青な空の風をふるわせて、脱穀機が一台だけ働いている。ルルルル。脱穀小屋のひさしの下に、頭を垂れた二頭の馬がいる。ルルルル。粉雪がぼんやり光り、遠くでりんと鐘が鳴ると、二頭の馬は首を上げる。そして、はなやかだった昔のように、よいギャロップで地面をけって、馬小屋へと帰っていく。
poems.gloss: Shaking the wind of the deep blue sky, a threshing machine works on alone: R-R-r-r-r. Under the eaves of the threshing shed stand two horses with their heads hanging down: R-R-r-r-r. Powder snow glimmers faintly, and when a bell rings clearly far away, the two horses raise their necks, and with the fine gallop of their brilliant days long ago, they head back to the stable.
poems.note: The noise of a machine and two tired horses who suddenly recall their younger strength at the sound of a bell. Classical grammar: ～たる = ～た before a noun, ～なりし = 'was', こそ…なれ gives strong emphasis; 疋 is a counter for animals.

poems.title: 早春散歩
poems.author: 中原中也
poems.paraphrase: 空は晴れていても、建物にはかげがある。春、早春は心をなびかせ、まるで薄い絹やハンカチのように、私たちの心を引きちぎり、ばらばらにして風に散らす。私はもう、まるで過去がなかったかのように感じる。少なくとも通りを行く人たちの前ではそうであるかのように感じ、風の中を吹き過ぎる外国人のような目つきをしている。しっかりしたもののようでもあり、すきま風にも消えてしまうもののようでもある。そうして、このさびしい心を抱いて、今年もまた春を迎えるのだということを、ゆっくりと、ここに春がまた戻ってきたのだということを、土の上の日ざしを見ながら、冷たい風に吹かれながら、土手の上を歩きながら、遠くの空を見ながら、僕は思う。思うことにもすっかり慣れてしまって、僕は思う。
poems.gloss: Even though the sky is clear, the buildings have shadows. Spring, early spring, makes the heart sway, and as if our hearts were thin silk, or a handkerchief, it tears them apart and scatters the shreds on the wind. I now feel as if I had no past, or at least as if that were so in front of the people passing by, and I wear the look of a foreigner blowing through the wind, as if I were something firm, and also something that would vanish in a draft. And so, holding this lonely heart, I realize that this year again I am greeting spring, that slowly, here, spring has come round again. Watching the sunlight on the ground, blown by the cold wind, walking along the embankment, gazing at the distant sky, I think this; so used to thinking that I simply go on thinking.
poems.note: Early spring feels both hopeful and unsettling, and the walker feels rootless, like a stranger in his own city. Historical and literary forms: やうに = ように, 如く = ように ('like'), さうして = そうして, 迎へる = 迎える, 思ふ = 思う.
